justification: Formed a fresh read of the current build, then checked it against both round-2 design majors. Both are genuinely fixed, not papered over. (1) The 'Picking between an array, a list and a view' section that used to be a table hiding its entire List<T> column at 390px is now a bulleted decision list; verified on mobile-dark part25-26 and mobile-light part25 that every bullet (Read/write, Append, Insert/remove, Contains/IndexOf, BinarySearch, and the six 'use this container when' bullets) shows both the T[] and the List<T> cost on screen, fully readable, no fade, no hidden column. This is a real structural fix, not a font-size tweak. (2) The two code walls are now genuinely paced differently: the opening traversal harness (66 lines) sits behind a collapsed <details>, immediately followed by a 12-line snippet excerpt of just the two loop-nesting bodies that differ, and the reader reaches the results table within one screen of the collapse; the Grids layout benchmark (110 lines, three near-identical Sum* methods) is likewise collapsed with three short snippet blocks showing only each layout's differing indexing line, then straight into the ranges table and discussion. Verified this rhythm on desktop-light parts 01, 15-16 and mobile-dark parts 01-02, 21-22: a reader on a phone now sees a paragraph, a collapsed-program affordance, a snippet, and a table in quick succession instead of three unbroken screens of scaffolding. Several round-2 minors are also fixed: the DropEvens exercise's for-loop header now wraps onto two lines and is fully visible (mobile-dark part19, matches the suggested fix verbatim); the three Best(n, () => SumRows(g, n)) style call sites in the tiled-grid program now break after the open paren and are fully visible (mobile-dark part09); 'The third field: catching edits during a loop' now sits directly after the DynamicArray field list and before the wrapper-speed benchmark, so the three-field structure reads as one unit (confirmed in the desktop-light-part01 'On this page' order and the part09-10 heading sequence); the console header strings that used to truncate mid-word ('ratio' -> 'r', 'Insert(0)' -> 'Insert') are effectively removed from the reader's direct view because their programs are now collapsed, and the visible replacement tables/output blocks use short headers that fit cleanly (verified 'Size/Ratio/Grid MB/Row ns/Col ns' on mobile-dark part03 and 'Layout/Rows ms/Cols ms' on mobile-dark part23, both fully on-screen). Figures 1-4 all read correctly and are correctly themed in every combination checked (desktop-light, desktop-dark, mobile-light, mobile-dark), colours and dashed/solid states hold, captions are legible and say what to notice, and mobileOverflowPx is 0. Not fixed, carried from rounds 1-2: inline citations to Drepper's paper ('Drepper, section 3.2', 'section 3.3.2', 'section 3.3.1') are still plain, unlinked text, not tied to the numbered Sources list; the mobile hero (title, 4-line description, byline, date row, INTERMEDIATE chip, collapsed TOC card, prerequisite card) still consumes essentially the whole first 844px screen; and there is still no visible scroll affordance on overflowing code blocks/tables at phone width, only the edge fade. Two small new clipping instances were found this round that neither prior critic flagged: in the 'offsets' program (id=offsets), the three $"  [0,1] {Gap(ref grid[0, 0], ref grid[0, 1])}"-style lines clip after 'ref gr', hiding the second index argument that is the actual point of each line, at 390px (mobile-dark part04); and in the tiled-grid program's closing Console.WriteLine, the two interpolated format-string lines ($"n={n,4}  col/row {col / row,5:F1}" and the tiled/row continuation) still clip at 390px even though the three Best(...) call sites immediately above them were fixed (mobile-dark part09-10). Both are minor: the output panel below each program shows the actual numbers either way, so no claim is left unsupported. The one number that moved against the article is Lighthouse performance, measured serially this run at 87 (report.json/lighthouse.json), down from round 2's provisional 91 and round 1's provisional 94, and below the pass gate's required 90; failing/near-failing items are First Contentful Paint 3.1s, Largest Contentful Paint 3.1s, back/forward cache blocked, ~255 KiB of document-request latency and ~11 KiB of unused CSS. The page has grown (35 code blocks and 4 figures now vs 28/3 at round 1, 5902 words vs 4486), which plausibly contributes, but FCP/LCP/bfcache/network-dependency-tree are shell-level metrics, not something the writer's Markdown can fix directly. Net effect: both majors that held the score at 7.9 are convincingly resolved, most minors are cleared, and what remains is a short list of true nits plus one shell-owned performance regression that keeps this just under a clean pass rather than a design-system defect.
